problem: It says vocabulary size is far smaller than the token count because it is counted after normalization. That is the wrong reason. The vocabulary (types) is far smaller than the token count because words repeat many times; normalization only trims the vocabulary a little further. A student will conclude that lowercasing is what makes the two numbers differ.
fix: Vocabulary size is the number of distinct word types, counted after normalization such as lowercasing. Because the same words repeat across a corpus, it is much smaller than the token count: 208,000 tokens may come from only a few thousand types.

problem: The terms shingle and Jaccard overlap are used before being defined, then used again in Quiz Q4. An ESL reader on a phone has nothing to fall back on.
fix: Add one line: a shingle is a contiguous run of 5 tokens from a document; two documents are compared by Jaccard overlap = |A ∩ B| ÷ |A ∪ B|, where A and B are their shingle sets. Values near 1 mean near-duplicates.

where: Section 2, sentence 'Do the split before any cleaning tuned on the test data.'
problem: The wording is circular: nothing should ever be tuned on test data, so the sentence does not tell the student what to do with the split and the cleaning steps.
fix: Say it plainly: split first. Any threshold a cleaning step needs, such as a language-filter score, must be chosen on training documents only. Steps that need no threshold, such as boilerplate removal, may run on all documents.

problem: Six bare numbers are printed with no units and no labels (1.56 and 1.248 in particular are MB, not characters). The student has to match them back to the steps by position.
fix: Print each with its label and unit, for example: raw tokens = 260000; raw characters = 1560000; raw size = 1.56 MB; kept tokens = 208000; kept characters = 1248000; kept size = 1.248 MB.
